chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Buck Clayton's lessons; Harry Edison asks
summary: Jonah brings Buck for four or five lessons before his Africa tour; Edison mentions it in Nice.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Then about a year later he said, 'would you do the same for Buck Clayton?' I said, well, I'd heard about Buck and I wanted to offer, I sent word to Buck that maybe I could help him. But, I said, it's the same kind of situation, I've known him and he knows me, and it's hard to have any faith in somebody that you've seen around, you know. So finally Jonah said, I bought him 20 whiskeys, I pulled his throat and turned him every way but loose. And finally he dragged him down to my studio, pushed him in and said, sit down and take a lesson. So I gave Buck about four or five lessons. I didn't have that much time, because he had to go to Africa on a tour, and I heard that he had a very upsetting experience in Paris, a lot of people had ridiculed him or booed or something, because he couldn't play.

Before. Then he sent me a card from Africa saying, I don't know how to thank you, everything is going great. And I felt so good about it. And last summer in Nice, Harry Edison spoke to me about it. I heard Harry Edison and I said, what's wrong with you? And he said, well, I just heard a lot about you from Jonah and Buck Clayton, maybe
you can help me. I said, you don't sound like you need any help, you sound all right to me. And we never had a chance to get together.
